messages:
maria: Heads-up — our sampleapp CI on macos-latest is failing on the first `pip install` step when installing redwood-sdk. Looks like cryptography is trying to build from source for arm64 and blowing up.

sam: Can you paste the error output?

maria: Sure, here's the pip snippet from the runner:
```
Building wheel for cryptography (pyproject.toml) ... error
  error: Metadata generation failed
  
  Caused by: Rust compiler not found, and the wheel for this platform isn't available.
  
  ERROR: Failed building wheel for cryptography
  Running setup.py clean for cryptography
  Failed to build cryptography
  ERROR: Could not build wheels for cryptography which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
```

tyler: Yep — classic: on macos/arm runners sometimes PyPI doesn't have a compatible prebuilt wheel so pip falls back to building the rust-backed cryptography from source. CI images usually don't have rust or the right openssl dev libs.

sam: Two obvious fixes: (1) install rust & openssl headers in the macos job, or (2) pin cryptography to a version that ships universal2/mac wheels. Both suck in different ways.

maria: We already try to be zero-setup for contributors. Adding rust on CI is fine, but asking local devs to install rust is not great. Pinning in pyproject.lock feels brittle and could break other envs.

tyler: Another intermediate workaround: in the workflow, for macos jobs only, run `brew install rust openssl` before pip. That keeps contributor docs unchanged and CI passes. We can hide it behind a matrix flag.

sam: Also `pip install --only-binary :all: cryptography` will force using a wheel and fail fast if it's not available (so CI is explicit). But if wheel missing it still fails.

maria: POV: the underlying problem is how we export the lockfile for CI. We export a generic requirements.txt from poetry on linux runners, then reuse it on macos. That can pin linux-only wheels and cause mismatch. Is there a way we can export platform-specific constraints?

tyler: Poetry has limited cross-platform export support. The pragmatic approach: have separate exported requirements per platform in our CI cache: linux-requirements.txt and macos-requirements.txt, generated on the respective runners and cached. That keeps installs deterministic per host.

maria: ok that sounds reasonable. For quick unblock, I'll add a small macos step to brew install rust and openssl and mark the workflow as flaky until we land per-platform requirements.

sam: Can you open a tiny issue in the SDK repo documenting the plan (macos quickfix + long-term per-platform export)? I'll link the CI job. :+1:

maria: Done — opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py-sdk/issues/402 with the CI log and proposed steps. Added a note for DX: avoid local rust requirement.

ci-bot: Workflow `macos-build (matrix: py310)` failed — see run/987654321 for logs.

tyler: Thanks — let's keep this thread in sync. We should also add a short note to the contributor guide about the macos CI quirk until we fully fix the export flow.

maria: Will do. Thanks all. :pray:
